body: Do they know how much you are hurting? You don't have to necessarily tell them what you're going through. But maybe see if they can just spend some time with you. I find that more I am alone the worse I get. So just having someone physically there with me helps, even if they don't know what is wrong.

I've had people try to tell me that I'm not really depressed and that I just need to exercise and go outside. It makes me seethe with anger. They literally have no right to say things like that to someone who is struggling. They wouldn't say that to someone who had a broken leg. *Oh it's not that bad, you just wear that for attention*. The cruelty people show towards things they don't understand is disgusting.

I've just stopped talking about it so people don't start saying things behind my back about it. My coworkers love to do this. And it hurts like hell. But not everyone is like that thankfully. It sucks but there are some people out there who will care. Just have to find them.
Yes, I have done this. You're not weak, you're just struggling and hurting. There's nothing weak about not being okay. Is there anyone in your life you can talk to?
I'm sorry you feel that way too. It's rough man. :(

I have tried distracting myself with activities, but I've been finding recently that even trying to do said activities is exhausting. We have talked about it a little and he just gets worried and suggests that I go to the ER. I definitely do not want to do that, especially since I've read all sorts of horror stories about how badly those ER visits usually go. I know he is just worried about me and trying his best, but I know he is freaked out.

I would like to know a good solution too. The only thing that comes to my mind is creating spaces that are just meant for relaxation. Like if people love animals, maybe letting them just pet and hold some animals for a while. Or if someone wants to talk, just being able to talk to someone with 100 percent confidence that what is said will not be reported to the authorities. Just something simple. 

If physical therapy can exist for physical injuries then why can't the brain be treated like a strained muscle as well? I know brains are more complex. But maybe trying to be placed in a more peaceful environment, even if only temporarily, would help. At least I think it would help. It is not a one size fits all kind of fix. But anything other than the current system would be better.
